title: Trump: Pentagon drops flu shot requirement for troops
description_short: Trump: Pentagon drops flu shot requirement for troops
description_medium: A May 29, 2025 memo from Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg changed when reserve troops were subject to the annual flu-shot requirement, setting a 30-day active-duty threshold. It did not remove the requirement for all troops. Its effect on vaccination-related pay is not clear from the description.
description_long: Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg’s May 29, 2025 memo set a threshold for when reserve troops on active duty would be required to receive an annual flu shot: 30 days or more of active-duty service. That is narrower than a blanket removal of the flu-shot requirement for all military personnel. The change concerned how the rule applied to reserve service and could affect people whose duty periods fell below the threshold. The timeline also alleges that the policy changed whether troops were paid when they received vaccination, but does not explain the compensation rules or how that consequence followed from the memo. The memo’s text is needed to identify the reserve categories covered and its effective date. Until those details are clear, the policy can be described as a change in the service threshold, not as a general end to vaccination requirements or a proven penalty for being vaccinated.

title: Trump DOJ claims no evidence of Epstein clients or murder
description_short: Trump DOJ claims no evidence of Epstein clients or murder
description_medium: In July 2025, the Justice Department released a memo saying its review found no Epstein “client list,” no evidence requiring a change to the official suicide conclusion, and no plan to release more documents. The memo said the review covered more than 300 gigabytes of data and thousands of videos and images. Earlier statements by Attorney General Pam Bondi about a client list on her desk prompted questions about the change in public messaging.
description_long: The Justice Department released a July 2025 memo saying its review of Jeffrey Epstein-related materials had found no client list and no basis to revisit the conclusion that Epstein died by suicide. The Trump File account says the review covered more than 300 gigabytes of data and over 10,000 videos and images; the department said it did not plan to release additional documents and would not pursue what it called unfounded theories. The memo’s conclusions came after Attorney General Pam Bondi had said earlier that year that an alleged client list was on her desk, and after FBI Director Kash Patel said he had reviewed the evidence and expected material to be released. The account also describes a missing minute in video from outside Epstein’s cell and Bondi’s explanation that the gap reflected a routine camera reset. These are the department’s stated findings and the officials’ explanations, not independent proof of every underlying claim. The event is the memo’s announcement and its decision to close further disclosure, amid unresolved questions about the video and earlier public statements.

title: Trump: CDC stops recommending six vaccines for children
description_short: Trump: CDC stops recommending six vaccines for children
description_medium: A January 5, 2026 HHS memo reportedly changed CDC recommendations for six childhood vaccines, with the reported change focused on ages 11 to 17. The listed vaccines include rotavirus, which does not fit that age range. The revised guidance is needed to establish which vaccines and age groups were affected.
description_long: A January 5, 2026 Health and Human Services memo reportedly directed a change to CDC recommendations for six childhood vaccines. The described change applied to most children aged 11 to 17 and named vaccines for rotavirus, hepatitis A and B, meningitis, influenza, and COVID-19. The combination raises a scope question because the entry does not explain how the rotavirus recommendation applies to that adolescent age group, or whether different age bands were involved. A change in federal recommendations can affect how clinicians discuss routine immunization, but the exact guidance matters: a revised recommendation does not necessarily prohibit access to a vaccine. The memo and updated CDC schedule are needed to state accurately which vaccines changed, for whom, and whether the agency removed recommendations or shifted them to another category. Those distinctions affect which families receive routine clinical guidance.

title: Trump fires all Presidio Trust board members
description_short: Trump fires all Presidio Trust board members
description_medium: Trump fired all six members of the Presidio Trust board on April 8, 2026. CBS reported that the trustees were appointed by Joe Biden and had not yet been replaced when the termination notices arrived. The dismissals followed Trump’s earlier executive order seeking to shrink the Trust’s functions. The Presidio Trust oversees the former military post and parkland in San Francisco.
description_long: On April 8, 2026, Trump fired all six members of the Presidio Trust’s board. CBS reported that the trustees had been appointed by Joe Biden and received termination notices that Wednesday; they had not yet been replaced at the time of the report. The dismissals followed an earlier Trump executive order that called the Trust unnecessary and sought to shrink its functions as part of a broader effort to reduce federal agencies. The Presidio Trust oversees the former military post and parkland in San Francisco. Its spokesperson said the board had expected new appointments and was awaiting information about replacements. Former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, who helped establish the Trust in 1996, criticized the decision. The reported action removed the full board but did not itself establish who would replace its members or how the Trust’s operations would change. It was a personnel decision within a federal entity, following the administration’s stated plan to reduce the organization’s role.
